title: Isaiah Chapter 31 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Isaiah chapter 31 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Isaiah Chapter 31 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Isaiah Chapter 31.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 31:1 say about those who go down to Egypt for help?
questions.correctAnswer: Woe to them
questions.explanation: Isaiah 31:1 starts with 'Woe to them that go down to Egypt for help', indicating a warning against seeking help from Egypt.

questions.question: In Isaiah 31:2, what will the LORD bring against the house of the evildoers?
questions.correctAnswer: Evil
questions.explanation: Isaiah 31:2 states that the LORD 'will bring evil' against the house of the evildoers.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 31:3, who are the Egyptians compared to in terms of strength?
questions.correctAnswer: God
questions.explanation: Isaiah 31:3 points out that 'the Egyptians are men, and not God', emphasizing their limitations.

questions.question: How does the LORD defend Jerusalem according to Isaiah 31:5?
questions.correctAnswer: With birds flying
questions.explanation: Isaiah 31:5 compares the LORD's defense of Jerusalem to 'birds flying', indicating His protective nature.

questions.question: What should every man do in that day according to Isaiah 31:7?
questions.correctAnswer: Cast away his idols
questions.explanation: Isaiah 31:7 instructs that 'every man shall cast away his idols of silver, and his idols of gold'.

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 31:4 mentions that the LORD will be afraid of the multitude of shepherds.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Isaiah 31:4 states that the LORD 'will not be afraid of their voice', indicating He is not intimidated.

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 31:6 calls for the children of Israel to turn to the LORD.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Isaiah 31:6 states, 'Turn ye unto him from whom the children of Israel have deeply revolted', encouraging repentance.

questions.question: What will happen to the Assyrian according to Isaiah 31:8?
questions.correctAnswer: He will flee
questions.explanation: Isaiah 31:8 mentions that 'he shall flee from the sword', indicating his defeat.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 31:2 say about the words of the LORD?
questions.correctAnswer: They will not return void
questions.explanation: Isaiah 31:2 indicates that the LORD 'will not call back his words', highlighting their permanence.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 31:9, who shall be afraid of the ensign?
questions.correctAnswer: His princes
questions.explanation: Isaiah 31:9 states that 'his princes shall be afraid of the ensign', indicating fear among the leaders.

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 31:3 states that the horses of the Egyptians are spirit.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Isaiah 31:3 clarifies that 'their horses flesh, and not spirit', indicating they are not divine.

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 31:5 mentions that the LORD will deliver Jerusalem.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Isaiah 31:5 states, 'defending also he will deliver it', confirming the LORD's promise to save Jerusalem.

questions.question: Which instruction comes first in Isaiah 31?
options: Look unto the Holy One of Israel
questions.correctAnswer: Look unto the Holy One of Israel
questions.explanation: Isaiah 31:1 advises against trusting in chariots and horses and emphasizes looking unto the Holy One of Israel first.

questions.question: What will happen when the LORD stretches out His hand according to Isaiah 31:3?
questions.correctAnswer: Both shall fall
questions.explanation: Isaiah 31:3 mentions that when the LORD stretches out His hand, 'both he that helpeth shall fall, and he that is holpen shall fall down'.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 31:4 compare the LORD's action to?
questions.correctAnswer: A lion
questions.explanation: Isaiah 31:4 uses the imagery of a lion to describe the LORD's strength and presence in battle.

medium.title: Isaiah Chapter 31 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Isaiah Chapter 31 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 31:4, how does the LORD of hosts respond when faced with opposition, as illustrated by the lion and young lion?
options: He roars louder and fights without fear
He runs away from the noise
questions.correctAnswer: He roars louder and fights without fear
questions.explanation: Isaiah 31:4 describes the LORD as a lion that is not afraid of the noise of the shepherds and will come down to fight for Mount Zion, showing His strength and courage.

questions.question: What imagery does Isaiah 31:5 use to describe how the LORD of hosts will defend Jerusalem?
options: As a lion guarding its den
As birds flying and passing over
As a fortress with strong walls
As a river that never dries
questions.correctAnswer: As birds flying and passing over
questions.explanation: Isaiah 31:5 uses the metaphor of birds flying to illustrate how the LORD will defend, deliver, and preserve Jerusalem, indicating protection and care from above.

questions.question: What is the call to action in Isaiah 31:6 for the children of Israel?
options: To turn unto the LORD from whom they have revolted
questions.correctAnswer: To turn unto the LORD from whom they have revolted
questions.explanation: Isaiah 31:6 calls the people to turn back to God, from whom they have deeply revolted, emphasizing repentance and restoration.

questions.question: How does the metaphor of the lion and shepherds in Isaiah 31:4 relate to God’s protection over Mount Zion?
options: God fears the enemies like the lion fears shepherds
God will be silent like a lion hiding
God will boldly confront and not be intimidated by opposition
God will negotiate peace with the shepherds
questions.correctAnswer: God will boldly confront and not be intimidated by opposition
questions.explanation: The lion’s fearlessness against many shepherds symbolizes God's confident defense of Mount Zion as described in Isaiah 31:4.

questions.question: What practical lesson about trust in God can be learned from the protection described in Isaiah 31:5?
options: Trust in military power for safety
Trust God's protective care like birds covering their young
questions.correctAnswer: Trust God's protective care like birds covering their young
questions.explanation: Isaiah 31:5 encourages believers to trust in God's care and protection, symbolized by birds that guard and preserve, teaching faith in divine protection.

questions.question: Based on Isaiah 31:6 and 31:7, what is the expected outcome if Israel turns back to the LORD?
options: They will cast away their idols of silver and gold
They will strengthen their alliances with Egypt
questions.correctAnswer: They will cast away their idols of silver and gold
questions.explanation: Verse 6 calls for turning to God, and verse 7 explains that this will lead to casting away idols, indicating repentance and spiritual renewal.

questions.question: How does Isaiah 31:4-6 teach about humility in relation to God’s strength?
options: We should boast in our own strength
We should fear human enemies more than God
We should humble ourselves by turning to God for help and protection
We should avoid confrontation at all costs
questions.correctAnswer: We should humble ourselves by turning to God for help and protection
questions.explanation: Isaiah 31:4-6 emphasizes God's power to protect and calls people to turn to Him, showing humility by seeking God's help rather than relying on human strength.

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 31:5 promises that the LORD of hosts will only defend Jerusalem but not deliver or preserve it.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Isaiah 31:5 states that the LORD of hosts will defend, deliver, and preserve Jerusalem, showing comprehensive protection.

questions.question: If a believer is struggling with fear of opposition, what truth from Isaiah 31:4 can offer encouragement?
options: God is silent in times of trouble
God will not be intimidated and will fight for His people
We must rely on our own strength to win
questions.correctAnswer: God will not be intimidated and will fight for His people
questions.explanation: Isaiah 31:4 portrays God as a lion unafraid of the noise of many shepherds, assuring believers that God will courageously defend His people.

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 31:6 instructs the children of Israel to continue in their rebellion against God.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Isaiah 31:6 calls Israel to turn to God from whom they have deeply revolted, meaning they should repent and cease rebellion.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 31:7 indicate about idols made by human hands?
options: They are a source of blessing
They are a sin and will be cast away
questions.correctAnswer: They are a sin and will be cast away
questions.explanation: Isaiah 31:7 says idols made of silver and gold by human hands are sins that will be discarded when people turn back to God.

questions.question: How does the passage in Isaiah 31:4-6 encourage believers to live in relation to God’s power and human opposition?
options: To rely on human strength and alliances
To fear opposition and avoid challenges
To trust in God’s protection and courageously face opposition
To ignore God and depend on material wealth
questions.correctAnswer: To trust in God’s protection and courageously face opposition
questions.explanation: The passage shows God as a fearless protector who will fight for His people, encouraging believers to trust Him rather than fear human enemies.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 31:5 suggest God’s defense over Jerusalem will be like?
options: Like a high wall that cannot be breached
Like birds flying, delivering and preserving the city
Like a powerful army standing guard
Like a river flooding the enemies
questions.correctAnswer: Like birds flying, delivering and preserving the city
questions.explanation: Isaiah 31:5 uses the simile of birds flying to depict God's protective care that defends, delivers, and preserves Jerusalem.

questions.question: What is the significance of the call in Isaiah 31:6 to 'Turn ye unto him' in the context of the chapter?
options: It emphasizes reliance on Egypt for help
It highlights the futility of trusting human strength
It promotes making idols for protection
questions.correctAnswer: It highlights the futility of trusting human strength
questions.explanation: Isaiah 31:6 calls Israel to turn back to God, contrasting with earlier verses that criticize reliance on Egypt and human power (Isaiah 31:1-3).

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 31:4-6 teaches that God’s protection requires us to be passive and fearful.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Isaiah 31:4-6 depicts God as a courageous protector who fights for His people and calls them to turn to Him, encouraging trust and courage rather than passivity or fear.

hard.title: Isaiah Chapter 31 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Isaiah Chapter 31.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 31:7, what will every man cast away in that day?
questions.correctAnswer: Idols of silver and gold
questions.explanation: Isaiah 31:7 states that every man shall cast away his idols of silver and gold, which were made for sin.

questions.question: In Isaiah 31:8, how is the Assyrian described as falling?
options: With the sword, not of a mighty man
By the hand of the Holy One
questions.correctAnswer: With the sword, not of a mighty man
questions.explanation: Isaiah 31:8 explains the Assyrian will fall with the sword, not wielded by a mighty or mean man, indicating divine judgment rather than human strength.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 31:9 say about the reaction of the Assyrian princes when he passes over to his stronghold?
options: They shall be afraid of the ensign
They shall make peace with Israel
questions.correctAnswer: They shall be afraid of the ensign
questions.explanation: Isaiah 31:9 states that the princes will be afraid of the ensign, symbolizing fear and defeat.

questions.question: Which metaphor is used in Isaiah 31:4 to describe the LORD's response to adversaries?
options: Like a lion roaring on his prey
Like a shepherd tending his sheep
Like a storm breaking the mountains
Like a fire consuming the forest
questions.correctAnswer: Like a lion roaring on his prey
questions.explanation: Isaiah 31:4 uses the metaphor of a lion roaring on his prey to depict the LORD's fearless and powerful intervention.

questions.question: What is the significance of the LORD defending Jerusalem 'as birds flying' in Isaiah 31:5?
options: It symbolizes swift and vigilant protection
It indicates the LORD's distance from the city
It refers to a festival tradition
It suggests vulnerability of the city
questions.correctAnswer: It symbolizes swift and vigilant protection
questions.explanation: Isaiah 31:5 likens the LORD's defense to birds flying, implying speed and watchfulness in protecting Jerusalem.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 31:6 urge the people of Israel to do?
options: Turn unto the LORD from whom they have deeply revolted
questions.correctAnswer: Turn unto the LORD from whom they have deeply revolted
questions.explanation: Isaiah 31:6 calls Israel to repentance and to return to the LORD, emphasizing their prior rebellion.

questions.question: In Isaiah 31:3, what two things are contrasted with the LORD's power?
options: Egyptians as men and horses as flesh
questions.correctAnswer: Egyptians as men and horses as flesh
questions.explanation: Isaiah 31:3 contrasts the Egyptians as mere men and their horses as flesh, not spirit, highlighting the LORD's superior power.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage echoes the theme of casting away idols as Isaiah 31:7 describes?
questions.correctAnswer: Jeremiah 10:14
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 10:14, like Isaiah 31:7, condemns idols made by human hands and calls for turning to God.

questions.question: How does Isaiah 31:8 foreshadow the downfall of the Assyrian empire in a way that reflects God's sovereignty?
options: By stating the sword will fall not by human might but by divine will
By describing a natural disaster destroying the empire
By predicting an internal political coup
questions.correctAnswer: By stating the sword will fall not by human might but by divine will
questions.explanation: Isaiah 31:8 indicates that the Assyrian’s fall is ordained by God’s sovereign power, not by human strength.

questions.question: What literary device is primarily used in Isaiah 31:4 with the comparison of the LORD to a lion roaring at his prey?
questions.correctAnswer: Simile
questions.explanation: Isaiah 31:4 uses a simile comparing the LORD to a lion roaring, employing 'like' to make the comparison explicit.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word for 'ensign' in Isaiah 31:9 most likely refer to in its cultural and military context?
options: A military standard or banner used as a rallying point
questions.correctAnswer: A military standard or banner used as a rallying point
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word for 'ensign' denotes a flag or banner, a key military symbol causing fear among enemies as in Isaiah 31:9.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage reflects the theme of God defending Zion as Isaiah 31:4-5 portrays the LORD's protection?
questions.correctAnswer: Hebrews 12:22
questions.explanation: Hebrews 12:22 speaks of coming to Mount Zion, echoing Isaiah’s depiction of God defending Zion.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 31:1, why is trusting in Egypt's horses and chariots considered a sin?
options: Because they do not seek the LORD, the Holy One of Israel
Because Egypt was under a curse
Because horses were considered unclean animals
questions.correctAnswer: Because they do not seek the LORD, the Holy One of Israel
questions.explanation: Isaiah 31:1 explains that trusting Egypt’s military power is sinful because they fail to seek the LORD.

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 31:6 calls Israel to continue relying on foreign alliances rather than turning back to God.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Isaiah 31:6 urges Israel to turn to the LORD, from whom they have deeply revolted, not to rely on foreign alliances.

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 31:9 indicates that the LORD’s fire in Zion and furnace in Jerusalem symbolize purification and judgment for the enemies.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Isaiah 31:9 uses the imagery of fire and furnace to symbolize God's purifying judgment upon enemies in Zion and Jerusalem.

theological.title: Isaiah Chapter 31 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Isaiah Chapter 31 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 31:1 warn against in seeking help?
options: Trusting in the Holy One of Israel
questions.correctAnswer: Going to Egypt for help
questions.explanation: Isaiah 31:1 warns that it is folly to go down to Egypt for help and to trust in chariots and horsemen instead of seeking the LORD.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 31:2, what will God do against the evildoers?
options: He will bring evil and not call back His words
He will provide them with peace
questions.correctAnswer: He will bring evil and not call back His words
questions.explanation: Isaiah 31:2 states that God is wise and will bring evil against the house of evildoers, demonstrating His justice.

questions.question: What is emphasized about the Egyptians in Isaiah 31:3?
questions.correctAnswer: They are men, not God
questions.explanation: Isaiah 31:3 emphasizes that Egyptians are mere men and not God, highlighting the futility of relying on human strength.

questions.question: How does God promise to defend Jerusalem in Isaiah 31:5?
questions.correctAnswer: As birds flying
questions.explanation: Isaiah 31:5 describes God's defense of Jerusalem using the metaphor of birds flying, indicating His protective and swift intervention.

questions.question: What should the people of Israel do according to Isaiah 31:6?
options: Return to the Holy One of Israel
questions.correctAnswer: Return to the Holy One of Israel
questions.explanation: Isaiah 31:6 calls the people to turn back to the LORD from whom they have revolted, indicating the need for repentance.

questions.question: What will happen to the Assyrian according to Isaiah 31:8?
options: He will be defeated by a mighty man
He will fall by the sword, not of a mighty man
He will make peace with Israel
questions.correctAnswer: He will fall by the sword, not of a mighty man
questions.explanation: Isaiah 31:8 states that the Assyrian will fall by a sword not of a mighty man, indicating divine intervention in his defeat.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 31:9 say about the fear of Assyria's princes?
options: They shall be afraid of the ensign
questions.correctAnswer: They shall be afraid of the ensign
questions.explanation: Isaiah 31:9 mentions that Assyria's princes shall be afraid of the ensign, which signifies God's power and judgment against them.

questions.question: What does the roaring lion analogy in Isaiah 31:4 reveal about God's character?
options: He is fearful of the enemy
He is indifferent to Israel's plight
questions.correctAnswer: He is courageous and unafraid
questions.explanation: Isaiah 31:4 compares the LORD to a lion unafraid of shepherds, illustrating His power and readiness to defend Zion.

questions.question: What doctrine is supported by the warning against relying on Egypt in Isaiah 31:1?
questions.correctAnswer: The sovereignty of God
questions.explanation: Isaiah 31:1 warns against seeking help from Egypt, emphasizing God's sovereignty over all nations and the foolishness of human reliance.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 31:7, what will every man do on that day?
questions.correctAnswer: Cast away their idols
questions.explanation: Isaiah 31:7 states that on that day, every man will cast away his idols of silver and gold, indicating a return to true worship of God.

questions.question: What attribute of God is demonstrated in Isaiah 31:2 by His actions against evildoers?
questions.correctAnswer: His justice
questions.explanation: Isaiah 31:2 demonstrates God's justice as He brings evil against evildoers, affirming His moral order in the universe.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 31:5 reveal about God's protection of His people?
options: It is conditional on their behavior
It is akin to a bird's flight
It is based on their military strength
It is only for a select few
questions.correctAnswer: It is akin to a bird's flight
questions.explanation: Isaiah 31:5 depicts God's protection of Jerusalem as like birds flying, showing His active and nurturing defense.

questions.question: What combined teaching do verses 4 and 5 convey about God's defense?
options: He uses human armies to fight
He is indifferent to His people's struggles
He fights fiercely and defends tenderly
He relies on the strength of the nations
questions.correctAnswer: He fights fiercely and defends tenderly
questions.explanation: Verses 4 and 5 illustrate that God will fiercely confront His enemies while tenderly protecting His people, showing His dual nature as both warrior and caregiver.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 31:3 teach about the nature of human strength versus divine strength?
options: Human strength is superior to divine strength
Divine strength is reliant on human efforts
Human strength is flesh and transient
Divine strength is irrelevant to human affairs
questions.correctAnswer: Human strength is flesh and transient
questions.explanation: Isaiah 31:3 teaches that human strength is merely flesh and not spirit, contrasting it with the eternal strength of God.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that reliance on God is irrational. What does Isaiah 31:1-3 actually teach?
options: Trusting in God leads to failure
Human strength is sufficient for protection
Relying on God is wise and essential
Idolatry is acceptable in times of trouble
questions.correctAnswer: Relying on God is wise and essential
questions.explanation: Isaiah 31:1-3 teaches that reliance on God is essential and wise, as opposed to depending on human strength which ultimately fails.
